Scalar optimization gives the necessary and sufficient threshold 2 r^(m+1) M_k(r)<=1. Szasz's sharp coefficient theorem and Enestrom--Kakeya give the fixed-offset formula in the stated zero-free range; the offset-three strengthening follows from a direct cubic Hurwitz test. All displayed root equations are strictly increasing in r, and the endpoint asymptotics follow from their logarithmic expansions.
